description: PWA foundation: add a hand-rolled web app manifest, an icon, link them from index.html, and register a hand-rolled service worker with a CloudFront-correct cache strategy. ZERO new dependencies (no vite-plugin-pwa / workbox). Static assets live in a new packages/frontend/public/ dir (Vite copies public/ verbatim to dist root). The SW makes the app installable ('Add to Home Screen') AND must update cleanly behind CloudFront without stranding users on stale HTML or a stale config.json/API URL. This feature leaves the app installable and the baseline build/tests green; no notification logic yet (that is FEAT-002).
steps: Create packages/frontend/public/ directory. Vite (base './') copies everything in public/ verbatim into dist/ at the site root, so these files are served from the CloudFront root.

Create packages/frontend/public/manifest.webmanifest (JSON): name 'AIモンスター育成 / AI Monster', short_name 'AIモンスター' (or 'AI Monster'), start_url '.', scope '.', display 'standalone', background_color '#1b2a4a', theme_color '#1b2a4a' (match the existing index.html theme-color and dark theme), lang 'ja', and an icons array referencing the icon file(s) below with maskable + any purpose. Keep it light.

Create a light icon asset in packages/frontend/public/ (e.g. icon.svg, a simple monster/egg glyph on the #1b2a4a dark background). An SVG keeps assets tiny and crisp; reference it in the manifest icons with sizes 'any' and purpose 'any maskable'. Optionally also add a 180x180 apple-touch-icon.png if trivially generatable, otherwise reuse the SVG. Document the icon approach in a short comment or README note.

Edit packages/frontend/index.html <head>: add <link rel='manifest' href='manifest.webmanifest'>, add <link rel='apple-touch-icon' href='<icon>'>, keep the existing <meta name='theme-color' content='#1b2a4a'> (do not duplicate), and keep <title>AIモンスター育成</title> unchanged. Use relative hrefs (no leading slash) consistent with vite base './'.

Create packages/frontend/public/sw.js: a hand-rolled service worker (plain JS, no imports, no deps). Implement a bumpable `const CACHE_VERSION = 'ddm-v1'` and a cache name derived from it. On 'install': call self.skipWaiting() so a new SW can take over promptly. On 'activate': delete all caches whose name !== the current CACHE_VERSION cache, then call self.clients.claim(). Implement a 'fetch' handler with these rules — (a) ONLY handle same-origin GET requests; let everything else fall through to the network untouched. (b) NEVER cache or serve from cache for config.json: detect requests whose URL path ends with '/config.json' and respond with a plain network fetch (no cache put, no cache match) so the runtime apiBaseUrl is always fresh — add a prominent comment explaining this prevents stranding users on an old API URL. (c) For navigation requests (request.mode === 'navigate') and HTML/index.html: use NETWORK-FIRST — try the network, put a copy in the cache on success, and only fall back to the cached copy when offline; this ensures a new CloudFront deploy's index.html (which references new content-hashed asset filenames) is picked up on the next online load rather than pinned stale. (d) For other same-origin static assets (the content-hashed Vite JS/CSS under /assets/, icons, manifest): use stale-while-revalidate (serve cache if present, fetch in background to update the cache) — safe because Vite filenames are content-hashed so a changed asset has a new URL. Guard all cache operations in try/catch or .catch so a failed cache op never breaks the response.

Add a thorough top-of-file comment block in sw.js documenting the caching strategy and EXACTLY why it updates correctly under CloudFront: content-hashed assets => new URLs on deploy; network-first HTML => new index.html pulled on next online load so it references the new asset URLs; config.json bypassed entirely => never stale API URL; CACHE_VERSION bump + activate cleanup => old caches purged; skipWaiting + clients.claim => the new SW activates without requiring all tabs to close (note the one-extra-load caveat for the very first SW install).

Register the service worker from the app, feature-detected and PRODUCTION-ONLY so local Vite dev is never affected. Prefer a small guarded effect in packages/frontend/src/App.tsx (or a tiny helper imported by main.tsx): if (import.meta.env.PROD && 'serviceWorker' in navigator) { window.addEventListener('load', () => navigator.serviceWorker.register(new URL('sw.js', import.meta.env.BASE_URL ?? '/').toString() /* or a relative 'sw.js' */).catch(() => {})); }. Use a relative path consistent with vite base './' so it resolves under CloudFront. Wrap in try/catch; a registration failure must be a silent no-op (graceful degradation).
Verify packages/frontend/vite-env.d.ts / tsconfig cover import.meta.env.PROD typing (vite/client reference already present). Do NOT add vite config plugins or new deps.
acceptance_criteria: packages/frontend/public/ contains manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, and at least one icon asset; after `npm run build -w @ddm/frontend` these appear at the root of packages/frontend/dist.
index.html links the manifest and an apple-touch-icon, keeps the existing theme-color meta, and keeps <title>AIモンスター育成</title> byte-identical.

sw.js is dependency-free plain JS: has a bumpable CACHE_VERSION, activate cleans old caches + clients.claim(), install skipWaiting(); fetch handler is network-first for navigations/HTML, stale-while-revalidate for hashed assets, and NEVER caches config.json (network passthrough).
SW registration is guarded by import.meta.env.PROD && 'serviceWorker' in navigator and wrapped so failures are silent; local dev (vite dev) does not register it.
No new dependency added to any package.json; vite.config.ts plugins unchanged.
`npm run build` succeeds and `npm test` + `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` remain green (>=152 / >=135).
verification: Run `npm run build -w @ddm/frontend` and confirm it succeeds and that dist/manifest.webmanifest, dist/sw.js, and the icon exist at dist root.
Run `npm run build` (full) and confirm all workspaces build.
Run `npm test` and `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` and confirm both are green at or above baseline.
Read sw.js and confirm the config.json bypass branch exists and that HTML is network-first.
findings: Implemented PWA foundation with ZERO new deps. Created packages/frontend/public/{manifest.webmanifest, icon.svg, sw.js}. Vite (base './') copies them verbatim to dist root; verified dist/manifest.webmanifest, dist/sw.js, dist/icon.svg present after build. index.html gained <link rel='manifest' href='manifest.webmanifest'> and <link rel='apple-touch-icon' href='icon.svg'> with relative hrefs; theme-color meta and <title>AIモンスター育成</title> kept byte-identical. Single SVG icon used (sizes 'any', purpose 'any maskable'); no PNG generated (kept assets tiny, documented in icon.svg comment). sw.js is dependency-free: CACHE_VERSION='ddm-v1', install skipWaiting(), activate purges non-current caches + clients.claim(); fetch handles only same-origin GET, config.json is pure network passthrough (never cached), navigations/document are network-first, other static assets stale-while-revalidate; all cache ops guarded. Thorough top-of-file comment documents CloudFront correctness. SW registration added as a guarded useEffect in App.tsx: PROD-only + 'serviceWorker' in navigator, registered on window 'load' via new URL('sw.js', import.meta.env.BASE_URL ?? '/'), wrapped so failures are silent; vite dev never registers it. BASE_URL is already typed via vite/client reference in vite-env.d.ts; no type additions needed. Verification: `npm run build -w @ddm/frontend` OK, full `npm run build` OK (all workspaces incl. infra), `npm test` 152/152, `npm test -w @ddm/frontend` 135/135. No package.json or vite.config.ts changes. No notification/Settings/i18n logic added (deferred to FEAT-002).
